newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt court sets insider trading fine - watchdog.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt court sets insider trading fine - watchdog.

text.p: Germany's federal securities watchdog, the BAWe, said on Tuesday that the Frankfurt District Court had ruled that a so-called "primary insider" should be fined for illegal insider trading.

The watchdog declined to name the individual concerned, which it said had been ordered to pay an immediate fine of one million marks. A total fine of 3.6 million marks was set, but payment of this was suspended pending a probationary year.
A primary insider is usually an employee of the company concerned in an insider trade.

The watchdog said the court case came about after the supervisory authority observed unusual trading activity in the stock of a firm before it announced in March 1995 that a foreign company had taken a majority stake in the company.
